root_idea.summary: The evidence preserves a midday-rest vocabulary alongside an authority branch associated with قَيْل, the title of a Himyarite king. The authority branch includes exercising rule or control.
root_idea.development: The root analysis treats the written ي as reflecting an original wāw, connects اقتالَ to the kingly title قَيْل, and regards the midday-rest vocabulary as a divergent branch. It also records a separate resemblance use in تَقَيَّلَ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized citation form مَقِيلٌ; the Quranic form is a substantivized passive-participial noun.
Displayed under the singular active-participle citation form قَائِلٌ; the supplied Quranic occurrence is its plural قَائِلُونَ.

senses.definition: A midday rest or siesta—the sleeping or resting period at noon.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran-focused lexical explanation allows the form to denote the act or period of sleeping at midday, as distinct from the place where that rest occurs.

senses.definition: A resting-place, especially a place of midday rest or siesta.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a place noun; in the Quranic occurrence it is understood as a favorable resting-place associated with the people of Paradise.

senses.definition: One who takes a midday rest or sleeps at noon; by extension in the lexical description, one who remains during midday.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural قَائِلُونَ refers to people sleeping or resting at midday. The recorded interpretation of remaining during midday is a closely related constructional gloss, not a restriction to a particular kind of person or object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A king or ruler, especially a king of Himyar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A historical royal title; its plural is أَقْيَالٌ.
A separate midday-related lexical use, distinguished from sleeping or resting at noon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exercise authority over someone or impose one's judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is explained by comparison with the authority of a قَيْل, a king or ruler.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rescind, dissolve, or annul a sale with the other party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a sale or purchase in a mutual cancellation or rescission construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To forgive or cancel a person's lapse, fault, or wrong action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used of pardoning a fault; the result may be described figuratively as raising the person from a fall.
The recorded construction is تَقَيَّلَ فلانٌ أباه, describing resemblance between a person and his father.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sleep or siesta taken at midday.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the midday sleeping period, distinct in headword from the active participle قَائِلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek the rescission of a sale or purchase.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when requesting that a completed sale be cancelled or rescinded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek pardon or release from a fault, lapse, or wrong action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when asking that a fault or lapse be passed over or forgiven.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A figurative seat or resting-place of an emotion, especially the heart as the resting-place of love or wrath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical application of مَقِيلٌ to the heart or another locus of feeling.

cautions: مَقِيلٌ has an evidence-backed ambiguity between the midday-rest activity or period and the place of that rest; the supplied Quranic context supports the place reading in 25:24.
The Quranic form قَائِلُونَ is presented under the singular dictionary citation form قَائِلٌ and is assigned the midday-rest meaning on the basis of the supplied lexical evidence.
The Maqayis passage mentions قِيل and قَال as nouns rather than verbal nouns but supplies no independent gloss for them; they are therefore not expanded into separate semantic entries.
